evals.prompt: Find me a 1-hour slot sometime this week during business hours
evals.expected_output: JSON output with available 60-minute slots during 9 AM - 5 PM business hours for the next 7 days, excluding weekends. Should include date, day of week, start/end times in 12h format, and ISO timestamps.
expectations: Output is valid JSON with a 'slots' array
Each slot has date, day, start, end, start_iso, and end_iso fields
All slots fall within 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM window
No slots appear on Saturday or Sunday
Duration of each slot is exactly 60 minutes
Query section shows duration_minutes: 60 and time_of_day: business
Timezone is America/Phoenix
At most 10 slots are returned (default max_slots)

evals.prompt: I need to find a 2-hour afternoon block tomorrow for a deep work session. Can you check my calendar?
evals.expected_output: JSON output with available 120-minute slots during 12 PM - 5 PM for tomorrow only.
expectations: Output is valid JSON with a 'slots' array
Query shows duration_minutes: 120
Query shows time_of_day: afternoon
Start and end dates are the same (single day)
All slot start times are at or after 12:00 PM
All slot end times are at or before 5:00 PM
Each slot spans exactly 2 hours
calendars_checked only lists calendars that responded successfully

evals.prompt: When am I free for a quick 30-min call this weekend? Morning would be ideal
evals.expected_output: JSON output with available 30-minute morning slots on Saturday and Sunday. Must use --include-weekends flag since weekends are now skipped by default for all filters except 'any'.
expectations: Output is valid JSON with a 'slots' array
Query shows duration_minutes: 30
Query shows time_of_day: morning
Start and end dates cover the upcoming weekend
All slot start times are between 8:00 AM and 12:00 PM
Each slot spans exactly 30 minutes
Uses --include-weekends flag since morning filter skips weekends by default
Output includes 'Arizona time' or timezone information

evals.prompt: hey can you check if I have anything open wednesday afternoon, need like 2hrs for a call with a client. just gimme one option per gap, don't need all the 15 min variations
evals.expected_output: Uses --compact flag to return one slot per free window. Duration 120, afternoon filter, single day.
expectations: Uses --compact flag in the command
Query shows duration_minutes: 120
Query shows time_of_day: afternoon
Start and end dates are the same Wednesday
Returns at most one slot per free window (compact mode)
All slots are in the afternoon (12 PM - 5 PM)

evals.prompt: i'm completely slammed tomorrow but my boss wants to squeeze in a 30 min 1:1. can you see if there's literally any gap?
evals.expected_output: Checks availability for tomorrow with time_of_day any to maximize chances of finding a slot. Duration 30.
expectations: Query shows duration_minutes: 30
Query shows time_of_day: any or business (either is reasonable)
Start and end dates are tomorrow
Output is valid JSON with slots array (may be empty if truly booked)
Timezone is America/Phoenix

evals.prompt: I need to schedule a half-day workshop next week, so I need a 4-hour block. Morning or afternoon works. Can you find me something?
evals.expected_output: Duration 240 minutes. Should check both morning and afternoon or use 'any' to cover both. Next week date range.
expectations: Query shows duration_minutes: 240
Start date is next Monday, end date is next Friday (or similar week range)
No weekend slots returned
Each returned slot spans exactly 4 hours
Output is valid JSON with slots array
